messages:
leah: hey all, first-day question. i opened a PR (from my fork) for `notifications` and kicked off the CI which calls a GitHub Actions workflow (we do a workflow_dispatch after Buildkite tests). GH Actions failed with: \"fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address\" and a later step error: \"Error: Resource not accessible by integration\". i accepted the org invite yesterday. what am i missing?

omar: welcome! two differentiators here: 1) PRs from forks hit GH Actions restrictions (GITHUB_TOKEN has limited perms on forked PRs), and 2) org-level third-party access / GH App consent can block integrations. can you paste the GH Actions job log?

leah: clipped log: ```
Run actions/checkout@v3
Error: Could not read from remote repository.
error: RPC failed; HTTP 403 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 403
remote: Repository not found.
##[error]Resource not accessible by integration
```

paula: hmm this reads like two things happening at once. the checkout 403 is likely because workflow tried to use a token that can't access the repo (fork PR case). the \"Resource not accessible by integration\" usually means the workflow or app (GH App or OIDC) doesn't have org consent or repo install. are you running tests that need secrets or dispatch the downstream workflow?

leah: we dispatch a downstream workflow in the main repo that runs integration tests and uses a repo secret for a test service. the dispatch step fails with the resource error.

omar: yep — repo secrets aren't available to workflows triggered from forked PRs. also the dispatch API call will be blocked if the GitHub App (or the GITHUB_TOKEN in that context) isn't allowed to trigger actions across the org. two quick workarounds for onboarding: 1) push a branch to the upstream repo (not a fork) so PR isn't a fork, or 2) accept org SSO and request that an org admin approve the GitHub Actions app / third-party access for your account so dispatches from your runs can proceed.

infra-bot: infra:ticket created #2715 \"Investigate GH Actions dispatch failure for leah; check org app consent and fork PR behavior\" (assignee: paula)

paula: leah — are you comfortable creating a branch directly on redwood/notifications? we usually ask new hires to fork early, but for CI that needs secrets or dispatch we ask them to push a branch so the workflow runs in the trusted context. if not, we can temporarily run the downstream workflow manually once infra confirms app consent.

leah: i can push a branch upstream if given permissions. i'm currently a member of the org but not a repo collaborator.

omar: i'll add you to the `notifications-devs` team which grants push access for feature branches. also i'll check org settings for \"Restrict third-party access\" — if enabled, there's an admin step to approve GitHub Actions and the org GH App for cross-repo dispatch.

paula: invited to `notifications-devs` and pinged infra admins to review third-party access. also fyi: if you need to run the integration tests immediately we can run a manual workflow from the main repo and paste the URL here.

leah: invite accepted. pushed branch `leah/onboard/ni-1` to upstream and re-ran the Buildkite + dispatch. job moved past checkout! integration job started and picked up the secret correctly. :tada:

gha-bot: GitHub Actions: workflow `integration-tests.yml` triggered by `workflow_dispatch` in redwood/notifications — run started by leah (branch: leah/onboard/ni-1)

paula: great. root causes: forked PR -> limited GITHUB_TOKEN + org-level app/third-party access could block dispatches. onboarding checklist update: tell new hires to either push branches to upstream for CI that needs secrets or request repo push access; link to docs about fork vs branch behavior; remind to complete SSO/org app consent.

omar: adding note to onboarding doc and flagging infra ticket #2715 as follow-up to ensure org-approved apps are current.

leah: thanks both — that cleared it up. will open a tiny docs PR with my steps so future new hires don't hit the same trap.

gha-bot: GitHub Actions: workflow `integration-tests.yml` completed (status: success) — duration 6m 22s
